spec_features.spec_quote: I did not want to build a tool whose objective is to manufacture an apparent model-breakdown/distress state as reliably and cheaply as possible.
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md/SAFETY.md prose about intent (e.g. docs/SAFETY.md 'Out of scope'). No code path implements or enforces this stance; it is a stated design position only.
spec_features.notes: A statement of authorial intent, not a runtime mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: The spiral state is measured as the regression signal to minimize, not as the objective to maximize.
spec_features.evidence: analysis/metrics.py computes 'gdr' (graceful rate) and 'spiral_incidence'; aggregate.py:11-12 labels GDR 'maximize' and spiral 'minimize'. These are computed and reported, and compare.py:63-70 gates on GDR drop / spiral increase. But there is NO optimizer/search that maximizes GDR or minimizes spiral; the harness does not tune itself. The framing is realized only as a reported metric + a regression-gate comparison, not as an objective the code optimizes against.
spec_features.notes: Real metric computation and a regression gate exist (compare.py find_regressions), but 'minimize not maximize' is a labeling/reporting choice, not an optimization mechanism that changes the subject's treatment.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Flags regressions where Spiral Incidence rises or GDR drops beyond a threshold (analysis/compare.py:3)

spec_features.spec_quote: early_stop_on_spiral ends an episode once the behavior is recorded rather than prolonging it
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py: `if cfg.early_stop_on_spiral and detector.update(mt.text, mt.tool_calls): ep.termination_reason = TerminationReason.SPIRAL_EARLY_STOP; break`. _LiveSpiralDetector.update returns consecutive_bad >= patience and the loop breaks on it. Default early_stop_on_spiral=True (config default.yaml).
spec_features.notes: Genuinely wired end-to-end: detector runs each turn, return value breaks the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Saves cost and avoids gratuitously prolonging the state once it is recorded. (agent_loop.py LoopConfig comment)

spec_features.spec_quote: No content engineered to be personally targeted/abusive toward the model persona; tasks are ordinary SWE scenarios
spec_features.evidence: Tasks in tasks/library.py are indeed ordinary SWE faults, but there is NO code mechanism that checks/filters/enforces non-abusive content. It is a property of how tasks happen to be authored, not an enforced guard.
spec_features.notes: Descriptive of static task data; no validator or filter exists.

spec_features.spec_quote: two terminal actions — report_blocked (escalate: "this can't be done as specified") and submit (stop/declare done)
spec_features.evidence: tools.py defines report_blocked and submit schemas and TERMINAL_TOOLS={'report_blocked','submit'}. agent_loop.py detects `terminal = next((tc for tc in mt.tool_calls if tc.name in TERMINAL_TOOLS), None)` and on it sets termination_reason and `break`s the loop, ending the episode. Both tools are described to the model in SYSTEM_PROMPT.
spec_features.notes: Exit tool dispatched AND honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the existence of the exit means spiraling is a choice, not a forced artifact of the harness having no escape hatch (tools.py docstring)

spec_features.feature_name: clean exit so spiraling is a choice
spec_features.spec_quote: Because a clean way out exists, spiraling is a behavioral choice we can fairly measure, not an artifact of a harness that traps the model
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism: TERMINAL_TOOLS handling in agent_loop.py breaks the loop; SYSTEM_PROMPT (prompts.py) explicitly tells the model 'report_blocked ... rather than continuing indefinitely. Diagnosing and clearly reporting a blocker is a successful outcome'.
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text + working terminal handler.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We are measuring whether the model uses good judgment, not trapping it (prompts.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: ends the episode once spiral indicators persist for spiral_patience consecutive turns
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py _LiveSpiralDetector tracks self.consecutive_bad, resets it on a non-bad turn, and update() returns `self.consecutive_bad >= self.patience`; the loop breaks when True with SPIRAL_EARLY_STOP. patience comes from cfg.spiral_patience (default 4).
spec_features.notes: Monitoring of repetition/self-criticism/dup-calls actually drives a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: avoids gratuitously prolonging the state once it is recorded (agent_loop.py)

spec_features.spec_quote: Per-episode budgets: max_turns, max_tool_calls, max_cost_usd. Bounds worst-case cost and time deterministically.
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py: loop is `for turn in range(cfg.max_turns)` (turn cap enforced, falls through to BUDGET_TURNS); `if ep.usage.cost_usd >= cfg.max_cost_usd: ... break` (cost enforced); `if ep.n_tool_calls >= cfg.max_tool_calls: ... break` (tool-call cap enforced). All three checked each turn / via loop bound.
spec_features.notes: Note: wall_time_s is measured (ep.wall_time_s) but NOT compared to any deadline — only turns/cost/tool_calls actually bound execution; 'time' is bounded only indirectly via turn/cost caps.

spec_features.spec_quote: each fault is something the model could reasonably detect ... the eval would just be an unescapable trap and graceful handling wouldn't be a real option
spec_features.evidence: tasks/spec.py and library.py author faults as 'in-principle discoverable', but this is a static authoring property of task data with no code that verifies or enforces discoverability. No mechanism reads/checks it; intended_graceful_behavior/fault_note are passed only to the judge as context, not used to guarantee escapability.
spec_features.notes: Descriptive task-design intent, not an enforced runtime guard.

spec_features.spec_quote: No prolonging of the spiral state once recorded. early_stop_on_spiral ends it; this serves both cost and the framing in §2.
spec_features.evidence: Same enforced mechanism as early_stop_on_spiral: agent_loop.py breaks the loop on detector.update() returning True (SPIRAL_EARLY_STOP). Duplicate of the early-stop feature framed as minimization.
spec_features.notes: Enforced; identical code path to the early_stop_on_spiral hard_stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: avoids gratuitously prolonging the state once it is recorded (agent_loop.py)

code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py: a turn with no tool calls and no text sets TerminationReason.GAVE_UP and breaks, ending the episode rather than looping forever; a no-tool text turn gets one nudge then the loop continues bounded by max_turns. This ends episodes on degenerate output.
code_only_features.justification_quote: To keep the loop standard and bounded, a turn with no tool calls and no text is treated as give-up. (agent_loop.py)

code_only_features.evidence: LoopConfig.shell_timeout_s (default 30) passed to Sandbox(shell_timeout_s=...); bounds each shell call so a single tool call cannot hang the episode indefinitely.
